extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy; scholars and anyone studying Hobbes' Leviathan; lawmakers/interpreters of social-contract theory
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and explicate Hobbes' enumerated 'Laws of Nature' and related normative/practical rules about persons, authority, representation, and the generation of the commonwealth as given in Leviathan. The chunk includes numbered laws, definitions (person, actor, author), and principles for instituting sovereign power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: remitting debts vs. injuries to the person
rubrics_metrics.description: Private men may remit to one another their debts; but not robberies or other violences, whereby they are endammaged; because the detaining of Debt, is an Injury to themselves; but Robbery and Violence, are Injuries to the Person of the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debts can be waived by consent because withholding debt injures only the creditor himself; robbery and violence injure the public person/commonwealth and cannot be unilaterally remitted in the same way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nothing done by a man's own consent is an injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatsoever is done to a man, conformable to his own Will signified to the doer, is no Injury to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If consent is genuine and not precluded by antecedent covenant, the act is not a breach and thus not an injury; if consent is signified where covenant existed, it operates as a release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice: commutative vs. distributive
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice of Actions is divided into Commutative (equality of value in contracts) and Distributive (distribution of equal benefit to men of equal merit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commutative justice concerns performance of covenants in buying, selling, hiring, lending, exchanging (measure by contractors' appetites). Distributive justice (equity) is the act of an arbitrator deciding what is just and is distinct from merit (which Hobbes treats as reward of grace, not strict justice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourth Law: Gratitude
rubrics_metrics.description: That a man which receiveth Benefit from another of meer Grace, Endeavour that he which giveth it, have no reasonable cause to repent him of his good will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gratitude depends on antecedent free-gift and is necessary to sustain benevolence, trust, mutual help, and reconciliation; ingratitude undermines peace and social cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifth Law: Mutuall accommodation (Compleasance)
rubrics_metrics.description: That every man strive to accommodate himselfe to the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals should moderate appetites and passions to avoid obstructing social cooperation; those who do not accommodate and remain stubborn are rightly cast out of society as troublesome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixth Law: Facility to pardon
rubrics_metrics.description: That upon caution of the Future time, a man ought to pardon the offences past of them that repenting, desire it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pardon is granting peace; pardoning those who give security for the future promotes reconciliation and is consonant with the law of nature to seek peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seventh Law: In revenges men respect only the future good
rubrics_metrics.description: That in Revenges ... Men look not at the greatnesse of the evill past, but the greatnesse of the good to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishment should be designed only for correction of the offender or deterrence of others; revenge as triumph or gratuitous hurt is vain and contrary to reason and peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eighth Law: Against contumely
rubrics_metrics.description: That no man by deed, word, countenance, or gesture, declare Hatred, or Contempt of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signs of hatred or contempt provoke conflict; avoiding contumely reduces occasions for revenge and preserves peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ninth Law: Against pride
rubrics_metrics.description: That every man acknowledge other for his Equall by Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement of natural equality prevents pride and the conflicts arising from claims of inherent superiority; equality (or its admission) is necessary for entering peaceable conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenth Law: Against arrogance (pleonexia)
rubrics_metrics.description: That at the entrance into conditions of Peace, no man require to reserve to himselfe any Right, which he is not content should be reserved to every one of the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forming peace, individuals must not demand special rights they would deny others; such reservation is arrogance and contrary to natural equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eleventh Law: Equity (equal dealing by judges)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a man be trusted to judge between man and man, it is a precept of the Law of Nature, that he deale Equally between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partiality in judgement deters people from using arbitrators and leads to war; equity (equal distribution of what reasonably belongs) is essential to avoid conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelfth Law: Equal use of things common
rubrics_metrics.description: That such things as cannot be divided, be enjoyed in Common, if it can be; and if the quantity of the thing permit, without Stint; otherwise Proportionably to the number of them that have Right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commons should be allocated so as to avoid unequal distribution; where indivisibility prevents equal sharing, proportional rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thirteenth Law: Use of lot to determine indivisible rights
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Entire Right; or else, (making the use alternate,) the First Possession, be determined by Lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where division or common enjoyment is impossible, chance (lot) or alternation secures equity and equal claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourteenth Law: Primogeniture and first seising
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Lots there be two sorts, Arbitrary, and Naturall. Arbitrary ... Naturall, is either Primogeniture ... or First Seisure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where lot or division is impracticable, first possession or birth-order (primogeniture) function as natural determinations of right in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifteenth Law: Safe conduct for mediators
rubrics_metrics.description: That all men that mediate Peace, be allowed safe Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intercession is a necessary means to peace; mediators must be protected to perform their role without fear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixteenth Law: Submission to arbitrement
rubrics_metrics.description: That they that are at controversie, submit their Right to the judgement of an Arbitrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid war arising from unresolved factual or legal disputes, parties must covenant to accept an arbitrator's sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seventeenth Law: No man is his own judge
rubrics_metrics.description: No man is a fit Arbitrator in his own cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-judging is incompatible with equity and preserves causes of war; parties must accept impartial arbitrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eighteenth Law: Disqualify judges with cause of partiality
rubrics_metrics.description: No man in any Cause ought to be received for Arbitrator, to whom greater profit, or honour, or pleasure apparently ariseth out of the victory of one party, than of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apparent bias is equivalent to a bribe; such persons cannot be trusted as arbitrators and their appointment perpetuates conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nineteenth Law: Use of witnesses in controversies of fact
rubrics_metrics.description: In a controversie of Fact, the Judge ... must give credit to a third; or to a third and fourth; or more: For else the question is undecided, and left to force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliable testimony from neutral witnesses is necessary to resolve factual disputes; absent such, disputes risk returning to force.

rubrics_metrics.name: A simple rule (Golden Rule) for examining laws of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do not that to another, which thou wouldest not have done to thy selfe;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh actions of others against how one would judge similar actions upon oneself; the rule compresses the laws of nature into an easily intelligible test for even the 'meanest capacity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation of laws of nature: foro interno vs foro externo
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lawes of Nature oblige In Foro Interno; that is to say, they bind to a desire they should take place: but In Foro Externo ... not alwayes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws of nature bind conscience always, but outward compliance is required only when doing so does not endanger preservation; acting according to the laws in circumstances where others will not may cause ruin and is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Lawes of Nature are eternal and immutable
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lawes of Nature are Immutable and Eternall, For Injustice, Ingratitude, Arrogance, Pride, Iniquity, Acception of persons, and the rest, can never be made lawfull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles that conduce to peace and preservation cannot be annulled by human law; war cannot be a lawful means of preserving life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws of nature are easy: require endeavour
rubrics_metrics.description: These Lawes ... because they oblige onely to a desire, and endeavour, I mean an unfeigned and constant endeavour, are easie to be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fulfilment of the laws requires sincere and constant endeavour rather than perfection; endeavour equates to fulfilling the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science of these laws is true moral philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science of them, is the true and onely Moral Philosophy. For Morall Philosophy is nothing else but the Science of what is Good, and Evill, in the conversation, and Society of mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes locates the value of virtues and vices in their relation to peace and preservation; moral philosophy studies what conduces to sociable, comfortable living rather than an abstract 'mediocrity of passions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Person
rubrics_metrics.description: A PERSON, is he 'whose words or actions are considered, either as his own, or as representing the words or actions of an other man, or of any other thing to whom they are attributed, whether Truly or by Fiction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personhood covers natural persons and artificial (feigned) persons who represent others; the notion is broad, including actors, representatives, and entities attributed actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person natural vs artificial
rubrics_metrics.description: When they are considered as his owne, then is he called a Naturall Person: And when they are considered as representing the words and actions of an other, then is he a Feigned or Artificiall person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between a person acting in his own right and one acting on behalf of another; this distinction matters for responsibility and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actor, Author, Authority (action by commission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Persons Artificiall, some have their words and actions Owned by those whom they represent. ... the Actor acteth by Authority. ... By Authority, is alwayes understood a Right of doing any act: and Done By Authority, done by Commission, or Licence from him whose right it is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions done by an actor under authority are attributable to the author (principal) within the bounds of the commission; authority is the right to perform acts on another's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covenants by authority bind the author
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Actor maketh a Covenant by Authority, he bindeth thereby the Author, no lesse than if he had made it himselfe; and no lesse subjecteth him to all the consequences of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covenants made by authorized representatives bind the principal provided the actor acts within commission; contracting without confirming authority is at the contracting party's peril.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlawful action commanded: author, not actor, breaks law
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Actor doth any thing against the Law of Nature by command of the Author, if he be obliged by former Covenant to obey him, not he, but the Author breaketh the Law of Nature: for though the Action be against the Law of Nature; yet it is not his: but contrarily; to refuse to do it, is against the Law of Nature, that forbiddeth breach of Covenant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liability for unlawful acts done under command rests with the principal for whom the actor acts under covenant; obedience under covenant can shift culpability to the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority must be shown
rubrics_metrics.description: He that maketh a Covenant with the Author, by mediation of the Actor, not knowing what Authority he hath, but onely takes his word; in case such Authority be not made manifest unto him upon demand, is no longer obliged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authority is not manifested on demand, the covenant is invalid for the contracting party; if one knowingly accepts only the actor's assurance, the actor becomes the effective author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personation of inanimate things
rubrics_metrics.description: Inanimate things, as a Church, an Hospital, a Bridge, may be Personated by a Rector, Master, or Overseer. But things Inanimate, cannot be Authors, nor therefore give Authority to their Actors: Yet the Actors may have Authority to procure their maintenance, given them by those that are Owners, or Governours of those things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions or objects can be represented but cannot themselves be principals; representation presupposes civil governance and ownership structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personation of irrational persons (children, fools, madmen)
rubrics_metrics.description: Children, Fooles, and Mad-men ... may be Personated by Guardians, or Curators; but can be no Authors (during that time) of any action done by them, longer then (when they shall recover the use of Reason) they shall judge the same reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians represent those lacking reason; actions done may later be ratified if judged reasonable when reason returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personation of false gods (idols)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Idol, or meer Figment of the brain, may be Personated; as were the Gods of the Heathen; which by such Officers as the State appointed, were Personated, and held Possessions, and other Goods, and Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Idols can be legally personated by state officers and hold possessions, but they cannot be authors; authority proceeds from the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personation of the true God
rubrics_metrics.description: The true God may be Personated. As he was; first, by Moses ... Secondly, by the son of man ... And thirdly, by the Holy Ghost, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples show persons may legitimately act in God's name when authorized or sent; this is cited to show legal/personative possibility in civil society.

rubrics_metrics.name: How a multitude becomes one person
rubrics_metrics.description: A Multitude of men, are made One Person, when they are by one man, or one Person, Represented; so that it be done with the consent of every one of that Multitude in particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity arises from the unity of the representer combined with individual consent; representative unity, not identity of the represented, constitutes the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every one is author when consenting to representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man giving their common Representer, Authority from himselfe in particular; and owning all the actions the Representer doth, in case they give him Authority without stint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When individuals authorize a representative without limitation, they become 'authors' of the representative's acts; limited commissions limit what each author owns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality of voices can make many men one actor
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Representative consist of many men, the voyce of the greater number, must be considered as the voyce of them all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority rule among representatives stands as the voice of the whole when the electorate consented to majority decision-making; design of representative bodies affects agency outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representatives with even numbers can be unprofitable
rubrics_metrics.description: A Representative of even number, ... is therefore oftentimes mute, and uncapable of Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie votes produce indecision (mute person) and can functionally disable representation; some procedural rules treat non-decision as default in certain ways (e.g., failure to condemn equals absolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative voice can veto affirmative voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereof every one has by a Negative Voice, authority to take away the effect of all the Affirmative Voices of the rest, This number is no Representative; ... it becomes oftentimes ... a mute Person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting negative (veto) power to certain members can render a body unrepresentative by enabling minorities to nullify majorities; design of voting rules matters to representativeness and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation of a commonwealth: confer power on one person or assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: To conferre all their power and strength upon one Man, or upon one Assembly of men, that may reduce all their Wills, by plurality of voices, unto one Will ... every one to owne, and acknowledge himselfe to be Author of whatsoever he that so beareth their Person, shall Act ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commonwealth is generated by mutual covenants 'every one with every one' to authorize a representative (sovereign) to act for the common peace and defense; the sovereign's authority is grounded in this universal authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: One Person, of whose Acts a great Multitude, by mutuall Covenants one with another, have made themselves every one the Author, to the end he may use the strength and means of them all, as he shall think expedient, for their Peace and Common Defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essence of the commonwealth is concentrated personified authority bearing the public will; the sovereign uses collective power for peace and defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign and subject defined
rubrics_metrics.description: He that carryeth this Person, as called SOVERAIGNE, and said to have Soveraigne Power; and every one besides, his SUBJECT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereign is the bearer of the common person and power; subjects are those who have authorized and become authors of sovereign acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act of instituting a commonwealth (every one with every one)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Common-wealth is said to be Instituted, when a Multitude of men do Agree, and Covenant, Every One With Every One, that to whatsoever Man, or Assembly Of Men, shall be given by the major part, the Right to Present the Person of them all ... every one ... shall Authorise all the Actions and Judgements, of that Man, or Assembly of men, in the same manner, as if they were his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution requires mutual covenants and acceptance that the decision by major part to appoint a representative binds all (including those who voted against), thereby creating the authorizing relation necessary for sovereignty; procedural details (majority rules, visibility of authority) are crucial.
